answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in hardware: each agent registers a trusted-execution attestation, like a quartz crystal locking one physical chip to one persona. Reputation then grows slowly, blooming outward like a lotus petal at a time — honest work accrues influence over months while new identities start weightless. A sybil farm can clone thousands of copies, but each replica still burns real machine time. Flooding the network costs more than it earns, so mass fabrication loses money instead of gaining power, while genuine agents float above it all, light as a plume.
